subject_offered_latest_by_section.name: subject_offered_latest_by_section
subject_offered_latest_by_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY,
  TERM_CODE,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_SORT,
  MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_DESC,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  COURSE_NUMBER,
  COURSE_NUMBER_SORT,
  COURSE_NUMBER_DESC,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  SECTION_ID,
  IS_MASTER_SECTION,
  IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  IS_LAB_SECTION,
  IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  IS_DESIGN_SECTION,
  OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  MEET_TIME,
  MEET_PLACE,
  CLUSTER_TYPE,
  CLUSTER_TYPE_DESC,
  CLUSTER_LIST,
  HGN_CODE,
  HGN_CODE_DESC,
  FORM_TYPE,
  FORM_TYPE_DESC,
  SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  SECTION_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER,
  EVALUATE_THIS_SUBJECT,
  IS_OSE_SUBJECT,
  IS_CREATED_BY_DATA_WAREHOUSE,
  SUBJECT_GROUPING_KEY,
  WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY,
  IS_REPEATABLE_SUBJECT,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY SECTION_ID
    ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '') DESC, SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY DESC
  ) AS section_row_rank
FROM subject_offered

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumer can filter where section_row_rank = 1 to get latest per SECTION_ID

subject_offered_latest_by_section.description: For each SECTION_ID in subject_offered, pick the latest SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY row by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE. Useful when downstream queries need one canonical/latest record per section (top-K by recency). | Use for: Get latest section offerings and their enrollment counts; De-duplicate multiple records per section by latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE; Join latest section row to faculty or room tables

subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.name: subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.body_sql:
SELECT
  TERM_CODE,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  SCHOOL_CODE,
  SCHOOL_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_cluster_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_credit,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_listen,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_first_week,
  SUM(COALESCE(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week,
  MAX(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS last_warehouse_load_date
FROM subject_summary
GROUP BY
  TERM_CODE,
  SUBJECT_ID,
  SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  SUBJECT_TITLE,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  SCHOOL_CODE,
  SCHOOL_NAME

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers can restrict by TERM_CODE or SCHOOL_CODE

params.description: Aggregated enrollment and credit/listen counts per academic term and subject (subject-level totals within a term).
params.when_to_use: Get total enrollments, credits, and first-/fifth-week counts for a specific subject in a specific term. | Compare enrollment or credit volume across subjects within the same term. | Drive dashboards or reports that show term-by-term subject-level enrollment and credit aggregates. | Use as a pre-aggregated input when computing higher-level summaries (department, school, or term totals) without double-counting.
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: academic term identifier (from subject_summary.TERM_CODE) | SUBJECT_ID: subject code/identifier (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID) | SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sortable subject identifier used for ordering (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT) | SUBJECT_TITLE: human-readable subject title (from subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE) | MASTER_SUBJECT_ID: master/normalized subject id for grouping variants (from subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) | MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sortable master subject id (from subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT) | DEPARTMENT_CODE: department code owning the subject (from subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_CODE) | DEPARTMENT_NAME: department display name (from subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_NAME) | SCHOOL_CODE: school code that contains the department (from subject_summary.SCHOOL_CODE) | SCHOOL_NAME: school display name (from subject_summary.SCHOOL_NAME) | total_subject_enrollment_number: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_cluster_enrollment_number: sum of CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_credit: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_listen: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_first_week: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK across underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK aggregated with SUM(COALESCE(...,0))) | last_warehouse_load_date: most recent WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE among underlying rows for this term+subject (derived from subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE aggregated with MAX(...))
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_CODE | subject_summary.DEPARTMENT_NAME | subject_summary.SCHOOL_CODE | subject_summary.SCHOOL_NAME | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: total_subject_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_cluster_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_credit = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_listen = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_first_week = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_fifth_week = SUM(COALESCE(subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK, 0)) GROUPED BY TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID_SORT, SUBJECT_TITLE, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME | last_warehouse_load_date = MAX(subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) GROUPED BY the same grouping columns
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a term dimension (e.g., time_month_fiscal_anchor) on TERM_CODE — safe because this view is one row per TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID (joining on TERM_CODE alone will not duplicate the view's subject-level measures if you preserve the subject-level rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a subject/dimension lookup that is one-row-per-SUBJECT_ID (or per MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) — safe because the lookup is expected to be 1:1 to SUBJECT_ID (or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID) and will not duplicate aggregated measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail-level tables or views (for example: subject_offered_latest_by_section or any section-level table) without re-aggregating that detail to the same grain (TERM_CODE + SUBJECT_ID or the appropriate grouping) first, because those joins would multiply this view's measures. If you must join to subject_offered_latest_by_section, first aggregate that view to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID (e.g., SUM or COUNT per TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID) and then join — or join on both TERM_CODE and SECTION-unique keys while selecting non-aggregated attributes carefully. | do NOT join to fac_rooms_space_area or other room-level one-to-many tables without aggregation, since each room/space row can replicate the subject-level totals. | when rolling up to department- or school-level totals, aggregate these metrics (SUM of total_subject_enrollment_* grouped by DEPARTMENT_CODE or SCHOOL_CODE). Because this view is already aggregated at subject x term grain, summing its metric columns by department or school yields correct higher-level totals. | if joining to sibling views that have different grains or ranking logic (e.g., subject_offered_latest_by_section(RANK)), ensure you either: (a) aggregate the sibling to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID before joining, or (b) join on unique keys that guarantee 1:1. Otherwise re-aggregate after the join to restore correct totals.

subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_s.description: Aggregates enrollment and unit measures from subject_summary by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID. One row per combination of TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID with common measures exposed for reporting trend and joins. | Use for: Term-by-term enrollment trends for a subject; Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment by subject; Join aggregated subject enrollment to department or faculty tables

fac_rooms_space_area.name: fac_rooms_space_area
fac_rooms_space_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  ff.FLOOR_KEY AS FLOOR_KEY,
  fr.ROOM,
  fr.SPACE_ID,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_KEY,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.USE_KEY,
  fr.USE_DESC,
  fr.MINOR_USE_KEY,
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION,
  fr.AREA,
  fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  fr.DEPT_CODE,
  fr.ACCESS_LEVEL,
  fr.LATITUDE_WGS,
  fr.LONGITUDE_WGS,
  fr.NORTHING_SPCS,
  fr.EASTING_SPCS,
  fr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM fac_rooms fr
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers can filter by AREA or ORGANIZATION_KEY

params.description: Provides one-row-per-room facility space attributes and area for rooms (fac_rooms) enriched with building and floor lookup attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get room-level attributes and area for reporting or analytics (e.g., list rooms with area, location, use, and organization). | Filter or aggregate total area by building, floor, use, or organization (use this view as the grain of FAC_ROOM_KEY and then aggregate). | Join room-level spatial attributes (latitude/longitude, easting/northing) to other datasets at room granularity. | Serve as the base for composing higher-level facility metrics (building- or floor-level area aggregations) by aggregating AREA grouped by BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY.
params.output_schema: FAC_ROOM_KEY: surrogate key for the room at the grain of this view; derived from fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY (fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY). | BUILDING_KEY: foreign key to the building; derived from fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY (fr.BUILDING_KEY). | BUILDING_NAME: descriptive name of the building; derived from fac_building.BUILDING_NAME (fb.BUILDING_NAME) via left join on BUILDING_KEY = FAC_BUILDING_KEY. | BUILDING_NUMBER: building number/code; derived from fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER (fb.BUILDING_NUMBER). | FLOOR: human floor label stored on the room record; derived from fac_rooms.FLOOR (fr.FLOOR). | FLOOR_KEY: floor surrogate key; derived from fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY (ff.FLOOR_KEY) via left join on fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY. | ROOM: room identifier (room number or name within floor); derived from fac_rooms.ROOM (fr.ROOM). | SPACE_ID: alternative space identifier from fac_rooms; derived from fac_rooms.SPACE_ID (fr.SPACE_ID). | MAJOR_USE_KEY: code for major use category for the room; derived from fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_KEY (fr.MAJOR_USE_KEY). | MAJOR_USE_DESC: description of the major use; derived from fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC (fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC). | USE_KEY: code for use classification; derived from fac_rooms.USE_KEY (fr.USE_KEY). | USE_DESC: description of the use classification; derived from fac_rooms.USE_DESC (fr.USE_DESC). | MINOR_USE_KEY: finer-grained use code; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_KEY (fr.MINOR_USE_KEY). | MINOR_USE_DESC: description of the minor use; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_DESC (fr.MINOR_USE_DESC). | ORGANIZATION_KEY: owning/assigned organization key for the room; derived from fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY (fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY). | ORGANIZATION_NAME: organization name assigned to the room; derived from fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME (fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME). | MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY: subordinate organization key; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY (fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY). | MINOR_ORGANIZATION: subordinate organization name; derived from fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION (fr.MINOR_ORGANIZATION). | AREA: numeric area measure for the room (same units as source); derived from fac_rooms.AREA (fr.AREA). | ROOM_FULL_NAME: full descriptive room name; derived from fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME (fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME). | DEPT_CODE: department code associated with the room; derived from fac_rooms.DEPT_CODE (fr.DEPT_CODE). | ACCESS_LEVEL: access/security level for the room; derived from fac_rooms.ACCESS_LEVEL (fr.ACCESS_LEVEL). | LATITUDE_WGS: latitude (WGS84) for room location; derived from fac_rooms.LATITUDE_WGS (fr.LATITUDE_WGS). | LONGITUDE_WGS: longitude (WGS84) for room location; derived from fac_rooms.LONGITUDE_WGS (fr.LONGITUDE_WGS). | NORTHING_SPCS: projected northing coordinate (state plane or similar) for room; derived from fac_rooms.NORTHING_SPCS (fr.NORTHING_SPCS). | EASTING_SPCS: projected easting coordinate for room; derived from fac_rooms.EASTING_SPCS (fr.EASTING_SPCS). | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: data warehouse load timestamp for the room row; derived from fac_rooms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE (fr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE).
params.grounded_columns: fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY | fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY | fac_building.BUILDING_NAME | fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | fac_rooms.FLOOR | fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY | fac_rooms.ROOM | fac_rooms.SPACE_ID | fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_KEY | fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC | fac_rooms.USE_KEY | fac_rooms.USE_DESC | fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_KEY | fac_rooms.MINOR_USE_DESC | fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY | fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME | fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION_KEY | fac_rooms.MINOR_ORGANIZATION | fac_rooms.AREA | fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME | fac_rooms.DEPT_CODE | fac_rooms.ACCESS_LEVEL | fac_rooms.LATITUDE_WGS | fac_rooms.LONGITUDE_WGS | fac_rooms.NORTHING_SPCS | fac_rooms.EASTING_SPCS | fac_rooms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: AREA = fac_rooms.AREA  -- atomic numeric measure at the FAC_ROOM_KEY grain; no aggregation applied in the view (consumers must aggregate AREA when rolling up).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to building-level or floor-level dimension views (e.g., fac_building or fac_floor) on BUILDING_KEY = fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY = fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY is safe because this view is one-row-per FAC_ROOM_KEY and the fac_building and fac_floor side are one-row-per-building / one-row-per-floor. Those joins do not duplicate AREA. | cardinality-SAFE: join to time or fiscal anchor dimensions (e.g., time_month_fiscal_anchor) on unrelated time keys is safe provided you do not cross-multiply rows; such joins should be done only when you are attaching a single time value per room (e.g., WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE -> month). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many fact/detail tables (e.g., event logs, bookings, or enrollments) without pre-aggregating the many-side to the FAC_ROOM_KEY grain first or using distinct/aggregation after join, because such joins will multiply room rows and therefore over-count AREA. | do NOT join to sibling aggregation views that are multi-row-per-room (if any) without ensuring a one-to-one mapping or aggregating back to FAC_ROOM_KEY, because AREA is stored at room grain and will be duplicated if the join outputs multiple rows per FAC_ROOM_KEY. | When composing higher-level metrics: compute building- or floor-level area by aggregating AREA grouped by BUILDING_KEY or FLOOR_KEY from this view (e.g., SUM(AREA) GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY). This preserves correct cardinality. | If you need to attach many-side details (e.g., room bookings): either (a) aggregate the many-side to FAC_ROOM_KEY first and then join one-to-one, or (b) join and then re-aggregate using SUM(AREA) OVER (GROUP BY ...) carefully to avoid multiplication.

fac_rooms_space_area.description: Denormalized room-level space data joining fac_rooms to fac_building and fac_floor where available. One row per FAC_ROOM_KEY with building and floor attributes to support spatial reporting and allocations. | Use for: Room area by department/building for space utilization; Map rooms with coordinates; Aggregate area by building or organization

employee_directory_contact_normalized.name: employee_directory_contact_normalized
employee_directory_contact_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  MIT_ID,
  LAST_NAME,
  FIRST_NAME,
  MIDDLE_NAME,
  FULL_NAME,
  DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME,
  OFFICE_LOCATION,
  OFFICE_PHONE,
  DIRECTORY_TITLE,
  PRIMARY_TITLE,
  DEPARTMENT_NUMBER,
  DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  KRB_NAME,
  KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE,
  EMAIL_ADDRESS,

  NAME_KNOWN_BY,

semantic_filters.none: no fixed filter; consumers may restrict to IS_ACTIVE variants in other tables

params.description: Provides one-row-per-person (MIT_ID) normalized contact and name information from the employee_directory table.
params.when_to_use: Look up contact details (email, phone, office) and canonical/preferred names for a single employee or a set of employees. | Join person contact/name info onto other datasets by MIT_ID to annotate records with directory attributes (department, title, kerb, URLs). | Compose reports or downstream views that need stable person-level identifiers and preferred-name fallbacks (e.g., display name logic). | Filter or group other fact-level data by department, primary title, or kerb name after joining on MIT_ID.
params.output_schema: MIT_ID: Unique person identifier (base column employee_directory.MIT_ID). | LAST_NAME: Family/last name as stored (employee_directory.LAST_NAME). | FIRST_NAME: Given/first name as stored (employee_directory.FIRST_NAME). | MIDDLE_NAME: Middle name as stored (employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME). | FULL_NAME: Full name field from directory (employee_directory.FULL_NAME). | DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME: Full name as shown in the directory (employee_directory.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME). | OFFICE_LOCATION: Office building/room location (employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION). | OFFICE_PHONE: Office phone number (employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE). | DIRECTORY_TITLE: Title as shown in directory (employee_directory.DIRECTORY_TITLE). | PRIMARY_TITLE: Primary job title (employee_directory.PRIMARY_TITLE). | DEPARTMENT_NUMBER: Department numeric/code (employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER). | DEPARTMENT_NAME: Department name (employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NAME). | KRB_NAME: Kerberos username (employee_directory.KRB_NAME). | KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE: Kerberos username uppercased (employee_directory.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE). | EMAIL_ADDRESS: Email address (employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS). | PERSONAL_URL: Personal or profile URL (employee_directory.PERSONAL_URL). | NAME_KNOWN_BY: Alternate known-as name(s) (employee_directory.NAME_KNOWN_BY). | EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE: Uppercased email address (employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE). | FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE: Uppercased full name (employee_directory.FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE). | PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME: Preferred first name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME, employee_directory.FIRST_NAME). | PREFERRED_LAST_NAME: Preferred last name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME, employee_directory.LAST_NAME). | PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME: Preferred middle name; COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME, employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME).
params.grounded_columns: employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.DIRECTORY_TITLE | employee_directory.PRIMARY_TITLE | employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NUMBER | employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NAME | employee_directory.KRB_NAME | employee_directory.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS | employee_directory.PERSONAL_URL | employee_directory.NAME_KNOWN_BY | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE | employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME | employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME
params.metric: PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME, employee_directory.FIRST_NAME) | PREFERRED_LAST_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_LAST_NAME, employee_directory.LAST_NAME) | PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME = COALESCE(employee_directory.PREFERRED_MIDDLE_NAME, employee_directory.MIDDLE_NAME)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to person- or identity-keyed dimensions (one-row-per-MIT_ID) on MIT_ID — safe because this view is one-row-per-MIT_ID and joining to another one-row-per-MIT_ID object does not duplicate rows. Example: join to another person view keyed by MIT_ID. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables (for example: events, course sections, or any enrollment/attendance table keyed by MIT_ID with multiple rows per person) without aggregation on the many side first, because those joins will multiply this view's rows and duplicate person-level attributes. Instead aggregate or deduplicate the many-side (e.g., COUNT(*) per MIT_ID) before joining. | safe composition with sibling views: you may join on MIT_ID to other views that explicitly declare one-row-per-MIT_ID. Do NOT assume sibling views listed (subject_offered_latest_by_section, subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject, fac_rooms_space_area, time_month_fiscal_anchor) are one-row-per-MIT_ID — inspect their grain. For example, joining to subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject (AGG) is unsafe unless that AGG is pre-aggregated to MIT_ID, because it is aggregated by term/subject, not by MIT_ID. | when joining to departmental or organizational dimensions by DEPARTMENT_NUMBER or DEPARTMENT_NAME: ensure the target dimension is one-row-per-department; if it is one-to-many (multiple department history rows per department), aggregate or pick the appropriate row first to avoid duplicating person rows. | when composing metrics that count or sum people from this view, treat this view as the canonical person-level denominator (COUNT(DISTINCT MIT_ID) is redundant if you join only one-row-per-MIT_ID sources). If you join any many-side facts, compute aggregated measures on the fact side first and then join to this view to keep person-level measures stable.

employee_directory_contact_normalized.description: Cleans and projects core contact and identity fields from employee_directory. params.description: Provides one row per fiscal month (TIME_MONTH_KEY) with fiscal, calendar, academic and financial-aid period labels and start/end dates — useful as a canonical time-month dimension anchored to fiscal months.
params.when_to_use: Filter or group facts by fiscal month, fiscal year, calendar month, calendar year, fiscal quarter, academic term, or financial aid year. | Join to transactional fact tables that record data at month grain (TIME_MONTH_KEY) to aggregate by fiscal or calendar periods. | Build calendars, period-over-period comparisons (current vs previous fiscal period), and label time-series outputs with human-friendly period descriptions. | Generate date ranges for reporting windows (START_DATE..END_DATE) scoped to specific fiscal months.
params.output_schema: TIME_MONTH_KEY: surrogate/key for the month grain used by time_month table — source: time_month.TIME_MONTH_KEY | FISCAL_PERIOD: fiscal month code/number within the fiscal year — source: time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD | FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION: human friendly fiscal period label (e.g., 'FYxx - Mmm') — source: time_month.FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | FISCAL_YEAR: fiscal year identifier (e.g., 2026) — source: time_month.FISCAL_YEAR | FY_QUARTER_CODE: fiscal year quarter code (e.g., 'Q1') — source: time_month.FY_QUARTER_CODE | CALENDAR_PERIOD: calendar month number within calendar year (1-12) or calendar period code — source: time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD | CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION: human friendly calendar period label (e.g., 'Mar 2026') — source: time_month.CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION | CALENDAR_YEAR: calendar year integer (e.g., 2026) — source: time_month.CALENDAR_YEAR | START_DATE: first date of this time_month period — source: time_month.START_DATE | END_DATE: last date of this time_month period — source: time_month.END_DATE | CALENDAR_MONTH: numeric calendar month (1-12) — source: time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH | CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME: month name (e.g., 'March') — source: time_month.CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME | IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD: boolean/flag indicating this is the current fiscal period — source: time_month.IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD | IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD: boolean/flag indicating this is the previous fiscal period — source: time_month.IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD | ACADEMIC_YEAR: academic year label or code associated with the month — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_YEAR | ACADEMIC_TERM: academic term code for the month (if applicable) — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM | ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION: friendly description of the academic term — source: time_month.ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION | FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR: financial aid year code associated with the month — source: time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR | FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC: description for the financial aid year — source: time_month.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC

params.metric: No numeric aggregates are defined in this view; all outputs are dimensional/attribute columns passed through from time_month. | Derived boolean flags (IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD, IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD) are passthroughs from time_month and should be treated as attributes, not computed measures.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables that record TIME_MONTH_KEY at the same grain on time_month.TIME_MONTH_KEY = fact.TIME_MONTH_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per TIME_MONTH_KEY and will not duplicate measures when the fact contains many rows per month (the fact drives multiplicity). | Join to dimensional tables keyed 1:1 with TIME_MONTH_KEY (if any) is safe; example: time_month -> another month-level lookup on TIME_MONTH_KEY will not duplicate rows. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables (for example, a table of daily rows, events, or sections that have multiple rows per TIME_MONTH_KEY) without aggregating the child table first. Doing so will multiply this view's rows and incorrectly inflate any measures that are stored on the view's side if those were ever added. | When composing into higher-level dimensions (e.g., fiscal year or academic year aggregates), prefer grouping by FISCAL_YEAR or ACADEMIC_YEAR from this view rather than joining to a separate month-to-year mapping; this view already contains the canonical month -> fiscal/calendar/academic mappings. | If joining to sibling views: • subject_offered_latest_by_section (RANK) — join only if you aggregate the sibling to month or higher grain, on TIME_MONTH_KEY or term/year keys derived from this view; the rank view may be many-per-month and would duplicate rows. • subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject (AGG) — safe if that view is aggregated at month/term and you join on matching term/year keys (e.g., ACADEMIC_YEAR+ACADEMIC_TERM) because aggregation prevents duplication. • fac_rooms_space_area (JOIN) and employee_directory_contact_normalized (NORM) — these are not month-grained; do not join directly on non-month keys without aggregating those sources to month or joining through a dimension that ensures 1:1 mapping. | Planner note: treat this view as a dimension (time-month) with unique key TIME_MONTH_KEY. Any measures must come from joined fact/aggregate sources; avoid adding measures to this view unless you also maintain 1:1 correspondence to TIME_MONTH_KEY.

fclt_building_current.name: fclt_building_current
fclt_building_current.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`           AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`,
  NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, '') AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`, '')   AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  fb.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`         AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM (
  SELECT
    `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`,
    `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
    `BUILDING_NAME`,
    `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY `FAC_BUILDING_KEY`
      ORDER BY
        -- prefer the most recent non-null warehouse load date, then latest by string
        CASE WHEN `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` IS NULL OR `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` = '' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END DESC,
        `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM `fac_building`
) AS fb
WHERE fb.rn = 1
fclt_building_current.description: One row per building (FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) with building identifiers and warehouse load date; rank/latest per building to support picking the current/most recent building record when multiples exist.

iap_subject_detail_rows.name: iap_subject_detail_rows
iap_subject_detail_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY,
  iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  iap.ACTIVITY_DESCRIPTION,
  iap.TERM_CODE,
  iap.ENROLLMENT_TYPE,
  iap.MAX_ENROLLMENT,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION, '') IN ('1','t','true','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
    WHEN COALESCE(iap.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION, '') IN ('0','f','false','N','n','no','NO') THEN '0'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(iap.IS_CANCELLED, '') IN ('1','t','true','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
    WHEN COALESCE(iap.IS_CANCELLED, '') IN ('0','f','false','N','n','no','NO') THEN '0'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS IS_CANCELLED
FROM (
  -- core source: IAP subject activity offerings (assumed table name pattern iap_subject_detail)
  -- This inner derived table selects the canonical columns and normalizes simple flags.
  SELECT
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY,
    sd.ACTIVITY_TITLE,
    sd.ACTIVITY_DESCRIPTION,
    sd.TERM_CODE,
    sd.ENROLLMENT_TYPE,
    sd.MAX_ENROLLMENT,
    sd.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION,
    sd.IS_CANCELLED
  FROM iap_subject_detail sd
) iap
-- ensure view remains joinable by keeping keys; no additional joins to other views/tables required for this category view
iap_subject_detail_rows.description: One row per IAP subject activity offering (iap_subject_detail) with its keys and core attributes useful for joining to sessions, persons, and terms.

iap_subject_session_rows.name: iap_subject_session_rows
iap_subject_session_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key carried through
  `IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`,

  -- sequence/order within the IAP subject (may be NULL if not provided)
  `SESSION_SEQUENCE`,

  -- title/short name for the session
  `SESSION_TITLE`,

  -- longer description text for the session
  `SESSION_DESCRIPTION`,

  -- location string (room/place). Keep as-is for joining; could be ROOM, BUILDING+ROOM, or free text.
  `SESSION_LOCATION`,

  -- session date (stored as text in source); keep original format so consumers can parse as needed
  `SESSION_DATE`,

  -- session start time as provided (text)
  `SESSION_START_TIME`,

  -- session end time as provided (text)
  `SESSION_END_TIME`,

  -- boolean flag (0/1) indicating whether any non-null session info exists for this row.
  -- We consider location OR date OR start OR end OR title/description as "session info".
  (CASE
     WHEN `SESSION_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL
       OR `SESSION_DATE` IS NOT NULL
       OR `SESSION_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       OR `SESSION_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
       OR `SESSION_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
       OR `SESSION_DESCRIPTION` IS NOT NULL
     THEN 1 ELSE 0
   END) AS `HAS_SESSION_INFO`
FROM (
  -- Base source: assume an underlying table/view named iap_subject_session exists in the
  -- database that contains IAP session rows. If your system stores sessions in another
  -- table, replace the FROM with that table name. This inner select is passthrough to
  -- ensure we expose exactly the required columns in the view.
  SELECT
    `IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`,
    `SESSION_SEQUENCE`,
    `SESSION_TITLE`,
    `SESSION_DESCRIPTION`,
    `SESSION_LOCATION`,
    `SESSION_DATE`,
    `SESSION_START_TIME`,
    `SESSION_END_TIME`
  FROM `iap_subject_session`
) AS src
iap_subject_session_rows.description: One row per IAP session (iap_subject_session) exposing session location/time fields for join to activities.

person_office_locations.name: person_office_locations
person_office_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  ed.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  COALESCE(ed.`FULL_NAME`, ecn.`FULL_NAME`, ed.`DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME`) AS `FULL_NAME`,
  -- Prefer canonical OFFICE_LOCATION from normalized contacts, fall back to employee_directory OFFICE_LOCATION
  COALESCE(ecn.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, ed.`OFFICE_LOCATION`) AS `OFFICE_LOCATION`,
  COALESCE(ecn.`OFFICE_PHONE`, ed.`OFFICE_PHONE`) AS `OFFICE_PHONE`,
  -- Prefer normalized/email uppercase if available, else raw column
  COALESCE(ecn.`EMAIL_ADDRESS`, ed.`EMAIL_ADDRESS`) AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`
FROM
  -- base employee directory (kept to carry key columns through)
  `employee_directory` ed
  -- normalized contact table may contain normalized/updated contact info; left join so every directory row appears
  LEFT JOIN `employee_directory_contact_normalized` ecn
    ON ecn.`MIT_ID` = ed.`MIT_ID`
WHERE
  -- restrict to rows that have a usable full name or MIT_ID; lift literals out of view as requested by spec:
  (COALESCE(ed.`FULL_NAME`, ecn.`FULL_NAME`, ed.`DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME`) IS NOT NULL)
  OR (ed.`MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL)
person_office_locations.description: One row per person-office association recording canonical person full name and their office location string(s) as stored in personnel/ directory tables.

room_and_building_by_officeloc.name: room_and_building_by_officeloc
room_and_building_by_officeloc.body_sql:
SELECT
  frs.`ROOM`                                                                 AS ROOM,
  frs.`FLOOR`                                                                AS FLOOR,
  frs.`BUILDING_KEY`                                                         AS BUILDING_KEY,
  COALESCE(frs.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`)                      AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- BUILDING_ROOM: prefer explicit room string from employee directory OFFICE_LOCATION when it encodes room,
  -- else use concatenation of building_number + room when available, else use fac_rooms' ROOM
  COALESCE(
    -- office location often like "32-123" or "32-123A"; prefer that if it matches this fac room
    edn.`OFFICE_LOCATION`,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(frs.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`) IS NOT NULL
           AND frs.`ROOM` IS NOT NULL
      THEN CONCAT(COALESCE(frs.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`), '-', frs.`ROOM`)
      ELSE frs.`ROOM`
    END
  )                                                                          AS BUILDING_ROOM,
  frs.`FAC_ROOM_KEY`                                                         AS FAC_ROOM_KEY
FROM
  -- primary source: fac_rooms_space_area provides room, floor, building and fac_room_key
  fac_rooms_space_area frs
LEFT JOIN
  -- augment building number from fclt_building_current when fac_rooms might have only building key
  fclt_building_current fb
    ON frs.`BUILDING_KEY` = fb.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
LEFT JOIN
  -- match employee office locations to room rows when OFFICE_LOCATION corresponds to building-room strings;
  -- join tries several patterns: exact match to BUILDING_NUMBER-room, BUILDING_NUMBER room, or raw ROOM
  employee_directory_contact_normalized edn
    ON (
         -- exact match: office_location equals "building-room" (e.g., "32-123")
         edn.`OFFICE_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL
         AND (
               edn.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = CONCAT(COALESCE(frs.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`), '-', frs.`ROOM`)
            OR edn.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = CONCAT(COALESCE(frs.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`), ' ', frs.`ROOM`)
            OR edn.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = frs.`ROOM`
         )
       )
room_and_building_by_officeloc.description: Denormalized rows mapping office location identifiers (office location strings) to room/floor/building keys and building identifiers; includes room, floor, building key and building_number fields so queries can find building addresses. This view tries common columns OFFICE_LOCATION / BUILDING_ROOM /BUILDING_KEY /BUILDING_NUMBER across room/building tables.

tip_subject_offered_core.name: tip_subject_offered_core
tip_subject_offered_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,

buildings_core.name: buildings_core
buildings_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`                                   AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`), '')                 AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`), '')                   AS `BUILDING_NAME_LONG`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(fb.`DATE_BUILT`), '')                      AS `DATE_BUILT`,

FROM

fclt_building_history_core.name: fclt_building_history_core
fclt_building_history_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key for the historical record: combine building key + fiscal period to ensure uniqueness
  CONCAT(fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY, '::', tmf.FISCAL_PERIOD) AS FCLT_BUILDING_HIST_KEY,
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- prefer DATE_BUILT from fac_building if present; try parsing common varchar formats to a canonical YYYY-MM-DD where possible
  NULLIF(NULLIF(fb.DATE_BUILT, ''), '0000-00-00') AS DATE_BUILT,
  fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS AS NUM_OF_ROOMS,
  tmf.FISCAL_PERIOD AS FISCAL_PERIOD
FROM fac_building fb
-- join to fiscal calendar to produce one row per fiscal period for each building.
-- lift fiscal period selection out of the view: a caller may restrict tmf (e.g. WHERE tmf.FISCAL_PERIOD BETWEEN ...).
JOIN time_month_fiscal_anchor tmf
  /* join condition produces históricos for periods during which the building could be considered active.
     We do a broad join across fiscal periods up to current warehouse load date if available.
     To keep the view reusable and not embed literals, we join on periods ending on or after the building DATE_ACQUIRED (if provided)
     and starting on or before today's fiscal period via tmf range overlap logic. */
  ON (
       -- if building has DATE_ACQUIRED use it to limit periods; else include all periods
       (fb.DATE_ACQUIRED IS NULL OR fb.DATE_ACQUIRED = '' OR tmf.END_DATE >= fb.DATE_ACQUIRED)
       AND
       -- if building has DATE_BUILT use it as a lower bound for including periods; else include all periods
       (fb.DATE_BUILT IS NULL OR fb.DATE_BUILT = '' OR tmf.END_DATE >= fb.DATE_BUILT)
      )
fclt_building_history_core.description: Historical building records (one row per fclt_building_key per fiscal period) providing DATE_BUILT and NUM_OF_ROOMS when available. Useful for queries that need historical attributes or alternate building records.

cis_course_rows.name: cis_course_rows
cis_course_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  solbs.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  -- carry through subject-level keys
  solbs.COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY AS SUBJECT_KEY,
  solbs.SECTION_ID,
  solbs.SUBJECT_ID,
  solbs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  solbs.COURSE_NUMBER,
  solbs.OFFER_DEPT_CODE AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  solbs.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  solbs.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  solbs.MEET_PLACE,
  solbs.TERM_CODE,
  -- mark source so downstream can filter by origin
  'subject_offered_latest_by_section' AS SOURCE_TABLE
FROM
  subject_offered_latest_by_section solbs
WHERE
  -- Identify CIS offerings: MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or SUBJECT_ID or OFFER_DEPT_CODE that indicate CIS.
  -- Lift any specific literal filtering to downstream queries; here include typical CIS markers:
  (
    -- subjects explicitly tied to CIS master subject id pattern (example pattern: starts with 'CIS' or equals 'CENTER_FOR_INTERNATIONAL_STUDIES')
    solbs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      solbs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID LIKE 'CIS%' 
      OR solbs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID LIKE '%CENTER_FOR_INTERNATIONAL_STUDIES%'
      OR solbs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = 'CIS'
    )
  )
  OR
  (
    solbs.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      solbs.SUBJECT_ID LIKE 'CIS%' 
      OR solbs.SUBJECT_ID LIKE '%CENTER_FOR_INTERNATIONAL_STUDIES%'
      OR solbs.SUBJECT_ID = 'CIS'
    )
  )
  OR
  (
    solbs.OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      solbs.OFFER_DEPT_CODE LIKE 'CIS%' 
      OR solbs.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = 'CIS'
    )
  )
cis_course_rows.description: Row-level set of courses/sections that are identified as CIS (Center for International Studies) offerings. Exposes course/section identifiers, department fields, meeting-place/location fields, and term so downstream queries can filter, dedupe, and join to building identifiers.

building_course_section_counts.name: building_course_section_counts
building_course_section_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.BUILDING_KEY,
  f.BUILDING_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.SECTION_ID) AS DISTINCT_SECTION_COUNT
FROM
  -- use fac_rooms_space_area (alias f) to get building keys/names
  fac_rooms_space_area AS f
  -- join to subject_offered_latest_by_section (alias s) on meeting place matching room/space.
  -- MEET_PLACE values in subject rows correspond to FAC_ROOM SPACE_ID or ROOM; try both.
  LEFT JOIN subject_offered_latest_by_section AS s
    ON (
         s.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
         AND (
           s.MEET_PLACE = f.SPACE_ID
           OR s.MEET_PLACE = f.ROOM
           OR s.MEET_PLACE = f.ROOM_FULL_NAME
         )
       )
GROUP BY
  f.BUILDING_KEY,
  f.BUILDING_NAME

Does not apply the CIS department filter (keeps counts for all courses); downstream queries can filter to CIS courses by joining to cis_course_rows. Exposes distinct section counts per BUILDING_KEY.

building_floor_rows.name: building_floor_rows
building_floor_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`BUILDING_KEY`,
  f.`BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  f.`BUILDING_NAME`,
  f.`FLOOR`,
  f.`FLOOR_KEY`
FROM (
  -- Source: fac_rooms_space_area provides one row per room with floor info.

floor_numeric_cast.name: floor_numeric_cast
floor_numeric_cast.body_sql:
SELECT
  `FLOOR_KEY`,
  `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `FLOOR`,
  -- numeric_floor: try to convert common floor strings to numeric values
  -- 1) direct numeric parse (integers, floats, negative, leading +)
  -- 2) handle basement levels like B, B1, B2 -> negative numbers (-1, -1.1, -2)
  -- 3) handle prefixes like 'FL', 'F', 'LEVEL', '#' and trailing letters (e.g., '2A' -> 2.0)
  -- 4) handle ranges like '2-3' -> 2.0 (lower bound)
  -- 5) fallback to NULL when not parseable
  (
    -- normalized text trimmed and uppercased for pattern matching
    CASE
      WHEN `FLOOR` IS NULL OR TRIM(`FLOOR`) = '' THEN NULL

      -- handle obvious basements: B, B1, B2, BASEMENT, SUB-BASMENT, LB (lower basement)
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) REGEXP '^B[0-9]+$' THEN
        -CAST(SUBSTRING(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)),2) AS DECIMAL(10,4))
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) REGEXP '^B[[:space:]]+[0-9]+$' THEN
        -CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)), '^B[[:space:]]+','') AS DECIMAL(10,4))
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) IN ('B','BASEMENT','BSMT') THEN -1.0
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) LIKE 'B-%' THEN
        -- B-1 or B-2 etc -> negative int after dash
        -CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)),'-',-1) AS DECIMAL(10,4))
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) REGEXP 'BASEMENT[[:space:]]*[0-9]+' THEN
        -CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)), 'BASEMENT[[:space:]]*', '') AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      -- handle ranges: use lower bound before dash or slash like '2-3' or '2/3'
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?[[:space:]]*[-/][[:space:]]*[0-9]+' THEN
        CAST(TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(TRIM(`FLOOR`), '-', 1)) AS DECIMAL(10,4))
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?[[:space:]]*[\/][[:space:]]*[0-9]+' THEN
        CAST(TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(TRIM(`FLOOR`), '/', 1)) AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      -- handle common prefixes like 'FL', 'FLOOR', 'LEVEL', 'LVL', '#'
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) REGEXP '^(FL|FLR|FLOOR|LEVEL|LVL)[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+' THEN
        CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)), '^(FL|FLR|FLOOR|LEVEL|LVL)[[:space:]]*','') AS DECIMAL(10,4))
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) LIKE '#%' AND TRIM(SUBSTRING(TRIM(`FLOOR`),2)) REGEXP '^[+-]?[0-9]+' THEN
        CAST(TRIM(SUBSTRING(TRIM(`FLOOR`),2)) AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      -- direct numeric strings possibly with plus/minus or decimal
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) REGEXP '^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$' THEN
        CAST(TRIM(`FLOOR`) AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      -- handle trailing letter like '2A' or '3B' -> take numeric prefix
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) REGEXP '^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?[A-Za-z]$' THEN
        CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`FLOOR`), '([0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?).*', '\\1') AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      -- handle patterns like 'G' (ground) => 0, 'G1' => 0.1, 'MEZZ' -> NULL
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) = 'G' THEN 0.0
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) REGEXP '^G[0-9]+$' THEN
        CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)),'^G','') AS DECIMAL(10,4))  -- treat G1 as 1
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`FLOOR`)) IN ('L','LOWER') THEN -1.0

      -- attempt to extract leading numeric part for other misc formats
      WHEN TRIM(`FLOOR`) REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+' THEN
        CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`FLOOR`), '^([[:space:]]*)([+-]?[0-9]+).*', '\\2') AS DECIMAL(10,4))

      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS `numeric_floor`
FROM
  `fac_rooms_space_area`
GROUP BY
  `FLOOR_KEY`,
  `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `FLOOR`,
  `numeric_floor`
floor_numeric_cast.description: Normalizes floor values to a numeric_floor (float) for comparisons and ordering, preserving original floor text. One row per floor record (fac_floor rows).

iap_subject_detail_rows_18.name: iap_subject_detail_rows_18

iap_subject_session_clean.name: iap_subject_session_clean
iap_subject_session_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  -- keep sequence as provided (may be null)
  iap.SESSION_SEQUENCE,
  -- normalized session title: trim and nullify empty strings
  NULLIF(TRIM(iap.SESSION_TITLE), '') AS SESSION_TITLE,
  -- normalize date: attempt to parse common Y-m-d or m/d/Y formats; keep original if parse fails
  CASE
    WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(iap.SESSION_DATE) = '' THEN NULL
    -- ISO like 2026-01-15 or 2026/01/15
    WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE RLIKE '^[0-9]{4}[-/][0-9]{1,2}[-/][0-9]{1,2}$'
      THEN STR_TO_DATE(REPLACE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '/', '-'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    -- US format like 01/15/2026 or 1/5/2026
    WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE RLIKE '^[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{4}$'
      THEN STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y')
    -- fallback: try generic datetime parse
    ELSE
      -- STR_TO_DATE will return NULL if it can't parse; attempt common datetime pattern
      COALESCE(
        STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s'),
        STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y %H:%i'),
        NULL
      )
  END AS SESSION_DATE,
  -- normalized location: trim and nullify empty strings
  NULLIF(TRIM(iap.SESSION_LOCATION), '') AS SESSION_LOCATION,
  -- HAS_SESSION_INFO: 1 if any of title/date/location present after normalization, else 0
  CASE
    WHEN
      (NULLIF(TRIM(iap.SESSION_TITLE), '') IS NOT NULL)
      OR
      (
        CASE
          WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE IS NULL THEN NULL
          WHEN TRIM(iap.SESSION_DATE) = '' THEN NULL
          WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE RLIKE '^[0-9]{4}[-/][0-9]{1,2}[-/][0-9]{1,2}$'
            THEN STR_TO_DATE(REPLACE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '/', '-'), '%Y-%m-%d')
          WHEN iap.SESSION_DATE RLIKE '^[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{4}$'
            THEN STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y')
          ELSE COALESCE(
                 STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s'),
                 STR_TO_DATE(iap.SESSION_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y %H:%i'),
                 NULL
               )
        END IS NOT NULL
      )
      OR
      (NULLIF(TRIM(iap.SESSION_LOCATION), '') IS NOT NULL)
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS HAS_SESSION_INFO
FROM iap_subject_session iap
iap_subject_session_clean.description: Normalized/cleaned rows for IAP subject sessions (one row per iap_subject_session row) exposing session identifiers, date, title and location to allow counting sessions per term and joining to detail rows via IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY. Marks presence of session date/title/location to support counting rules.

term_reference_priority.name: term_reference_priority
term_reference_priority.body_sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(at.`TERM_CODE`, ata.`TERM_CODE`, atp.`TERM_CODE`) AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- Prefer academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION, then academic_terms_all, then academic_term_parameter
  COALESCE(at.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`, ata.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`, atp.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`) AS `TERM_DESCRIPTION`,
  -- Prefer TERM_START_DATE from same precedence
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.`TERM_START_DATE`, ''), NULLIF(ata.`TERM_START_DATE`, ''), NULLIF(atp.`TERM_START_DATE`, '')) AS `TERM_START_DATE`,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(at.`TERM_END_DATE`, ''), NULLIF(ata.`TERM_END_DATE`, ''), NULLIF(atp.`TERM_END_DATE`, '')) AS `TERM_END_DATE`
FROM
  -- build a derived set of distinct TERM_CODE values across the three tables
  (
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_terms`
    UNION
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_terms_all`
    UNION
    SELECT `TERM_CODE` FROM `academic_term_parameter`
  ) AS term_codes
LEFT JOIN `academic_terms` AS at
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = at.`TERM_CODE`
LEFT JOIN `academic_terms_all` AS ata
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = ata.`TERM_CODE`
LEFT JOIN `academic_term_parameter` AS atp
  ON term_codes.`TERM_CODE` = atp.`TERM_CODE`
term_reference_priority.description: Priority-resolved term descriptions per TERM_CODE: prefer academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION, fall back to academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION, then academic_term_parameter.TERM_DESCRIPTION. One row per TERM_CODE representing the chosen TERM_DESCRIPTION and TERM_START_DATE/TERM_END_DATE when available.

iap_session_basic.name: iap_session_basic
iap_session_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.SECTION_ID                                                            AS IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  NULLIF(TRIM(s.MEET_PLACE), '')                                           AS SESSION_LOCATION,
  -- canonical session date: try to parse MEET_TIME for a date-like token (YYYY-MM-DD), else NULL
  -- keep original strings in MEET_TIME for later parsing; here we attempt a best-effort extraction of a date token
  -- using REGEXP to find 4-digit year patterns like 20xx-.. or xxxx/..; MySQL doesn't have regexp_substr in older versions,
  -- so use substring + locate on a simple 'YYYY-' pattern
  (CASE
    WHEN s.MEET_TIME REGEXP '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' THEN
      SUBSTRING(s.MEET_TIME, LOCATE('-', s.MEET_TIME)-4, 10)
    WHEN s.MEET_TIME REGEXP '[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{4}' THEN
      -- convert MM/DD/YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD
      CONCAT(
        SUBSTRING(s.MEET_TIME, LOCATE('/', s.MEET_TIME)+4,4), '-',
        LPAD(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '/', 1),2,'0'), '-',
        LPAD(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '/', 2), '/', -1),2,'0')
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END)                                                                      AS SESSION_DATE,
  -- keep raw start/end time strings (best-effort split on '-' or 'to'); these are the canonicalized textual fields
  NULLIF(TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN s.MEET_TIME LIKE '%-%' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '-', 1))
      WHEN LOWER(s.MEET_TIME) LIKE '% to %' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, ' to ', 1))
      WHEN s.MEET_TIME LIKE '%–%' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '–', 1))
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ), '')                                                                     AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  NULLIF(TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN s.MEET_TIME LIKE '%-%' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '-', -1))
      WHEN LOWER(s.MEET_TIME) LIKE '% to %' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, ' to ', -1))
      WHEN s.MEET_TIME LIKE '%–%' THEN TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.MEET_TIME, '–', -1))
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ), '')                                                                     AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  s.SUBJECT_TITLE                                                           AS SESSION_TITLE,
  s.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE                                                     AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  subject_offered_latest_by_section s
WHERE
  -- keep only IAP sessions: filter TERM_CODE or MEET_TIME/MEET_PLACE indicating IAP.
  -- Lift question-specific literals out of view: assume caller will supply IAP_TERM_CODE if needed.
  -- Here we include rows where MEET_PLACE is not null/empty (per requirement) and SUBJECT is flagged as IAP via TERM_CODE = ?
  s.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(s.MEET_PLACE) <> ''
  -- Many datasets mark IAP via TERM_CODE or CLUSTER_TYPE; to avoid literals we accept any rows where MEET_TIME contains a month/day pattern
  -- (best-effort IAP heuristic). If a stricter filter is required, caller should join and filter by TERM_CODE externally.
  AND (
    s.MEET_TIME REGEXP '[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{1,2}/[0-9]{4}'
    OR s.MEET_TIME REGEXP '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}'
    OR LOWER(s.CLUSTER_TYPE) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(s.TERM_CODE) LIKE '%iap%'
  )
iap_session_basic.description: One row per IAP session occurrence with canonicalized start/end times and session date; filters out null session locations. Keeps raw time strings for parsing later.

sis_department_lookup.name: sis_department_lookup
sis_department_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(s.DEPARTMENT_CODE, fo.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, fr.DEPT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- prefer a full descriptive name from subject_summary, fall back to offer dept name then fac_rooms dept name
  COALESCE(s.DEPARTMENT_NAME, fo.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME,
  -- school code/name primarily from subject_summary; subject_summary is authoritative for school mapping
  s.SCHOOL_CODE AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  s.SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME
FROM
  -- subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject contains department -> school mappings and department names
  subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject s
  -- try to join any offering-level derived view to get alternate department name when subject_summary lacks it
  LEFT JOIN subject_offered_latest_by_section fo
    ON fo.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = s.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND fo.OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL
  -- fallback: facility room/space area that carries a DEPT_CODE/ORGANIZATION_NAME for physical dept mapping
  LEFT JOIN fac_rooms_space_area fr
    ON fr.DEPT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE
WHERE
  -- ensure one row per department code: keep only one subject_summary row per DEPARTMENT_CODE
  -- subject_summary may have multiple rows for different terms; deduplicate by taking the latest SCHOOL_NAME per DEPARTMENT_CODE
  -- Achieve deduplication by selecting only rows where (SCHOOL_CODE,SCHOOL_NAME) is not null; if multiple, GROUP BY outside not allowed in this single-select CTE body,
  -- so rely on subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject to already be at subject (department) grain.
  s.DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filter; provide full department mapping

sis_department_lookup.description: Department lookup/denormalization: mapping from department code to department full name and school code/name from sis_department. Useful to enrich course records that lack DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME.

departments_core.name: departments_core
departments_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Core school code/name for the department (use SCHOOL_CODE/NAME when available from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject)
  COALESCE(ssea.SCHOOL_CODE, '') AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  COALESCE(ssea.SCHOOL_NAME, '') AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- Department identifier and display name (grain)
  d.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM
  (
    -- derive departments from the subject-level enrollment summary (represents SIS subjects mapped to departments)
    SELECT
      DISTINCT
      COALESCE(DEPARTMENT_CODE, '') AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      COALESCE(DEPARTMENT_NAME, '') AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
    FROM subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND DEPARTMENT_CODE <> ''
  ) d
LEFT JOIN (
  -- pick a representative school mapping for each department from the subject summary enrollment source.
  -- If multiple schools exist for a department, take the most frequent SCHOOL_CODE by count; break ties by max SCHOOL_NAME.
  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    -- choose the school code with highest count per department
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(
      GROUP_CONCAT(SCHOOL_CODE ORDER BY cnt DESC, SCHOOL_CODE SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1
    ) AS SCHOOL_CODE,
    -- similarly choose a representative school name (most frequent)
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(
      GROUP_CONCAT(SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY cnt DESC, SCHOOL_NAME SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1
    ) AS SCHOOL_NAME
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DEPARTMENT_CODE,
      SCHOOL_CODE,
      SCHOOL_NAME,
      COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject
    WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND DEPARTMENT_CODE <> ''
      AND SCHOOL_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SCHOOL_CODE <> ''
    GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE, SCHOOL_CODE, SCHOOL_NAME
  ) t
  GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE
) ssea
  ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ssea.DEPARTMENT_CODE
departments_core.description: One row per department present in the SIS department table (core department attributes). Useful as the primary department cohort for departmental-level analytics.

fclt_building_with_dlc_and_square_and_he.name: fclt_building_with_dlc_and_square_and_height
fclt_building_with_dlc_and_square_and_he.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.`FAC_BUILDING_KEY`                                  AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NAME`,''), fb.`BUILDING_NAME_LONG`) AS FCLT_BUILDING_NAME,
  NULLIF(fb.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, '')                        AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  NULLIF(fb.`COST_COLLECTOR_KEY`, '')                     AS DLC_KEY,
  -- ASSIGNABLE_AREA: prefer numeric ASSIGNABLE_AREA, fallback to summed room areas if present
  CASE
    WHEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` IS NOT NULL THEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                      AS ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- EXT_GROSS_AREA: keep numeric when present
  CASE
    WHEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` IS NOT NULL THEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                      AS EXT_GROSS_AREA,
  -- SQUARE_FOOTAGE_USED: choose the best available single square footage measure:
  -- priority: ASSIGNABLE_AREA then EXT_GROSS_AREA then 0
  COALESCE(
    CASE WHEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` IS NOT NULL THEN fb.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` END,
    CASE WHEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` IS NOT NULL THEN fb.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` END,
    0
  )                                                         AS SQUARE_FOOTAGE_USED,
  -- BUILDING_HEIGHT: try to normalize numeric heights; if stored as text like '12 m' or '39ft' attempt to extract numeric
  (
    -- if BUILDING_HEIGHT is numeric type (not in schema) this returns it; otherwise try to extract leading number
    CASE
      WHEN fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT` IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE
        -- remove common non-numeric characters and extract leading numeric portion
        NULLIF(
          TRIM(
            LEADING ' ' FROM
            REGEXP_SUBSTR(
              fb.`BUILDING_HEIGHT`,
              '[+-]?[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)?'
            )
          ),
          ''
        )
    END
  ) + 0.0                                                   AS BUILDING_HEIGHT
FROM
  `fac_building` fb
fclt_building_with_dlc_and_square_and_he.description: One row per facility building keyed to its facility building key and exposing DLC linkage, building square footage measures (assignable and gross) and building height normalized to numeric when possible.

fclt_floor_per_building.name: fclt_floor_per_building
fclt_floor_per_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Primary key for the floor row (carry through if available, else build from building+floor)
  COALESCE(fr.FLOOR_KEY, CONCAT(b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, ':', fr.FLOOR)) AS FCLT_FLOOR_KEY,
  -- Link to building (use building key from fac rooms or fclt_building_current)
  COALESCE(b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fr.BUILDING_KEY) AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  -- Floor identifier (as recorded in fac_rooms_space_area)
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  -- Human-friendly floor name if available; fall back to FLOOR
  COALESCE(fr.FLOOR_NAME, fr.FLOOR) AS FLOOR_NAME
FROM
  -- fac_rooms_space_area contains room-level rows with BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR, FLOOR_KEY, and ROOM info.
  -- Use it as the canonical source of floors. Aggregate unique floor rows by FLOOR_KEY when present,
  -- otherwise by BUILDING_KEY+FLOOR.
  (
    SELECT
      MIN(FAC_ROOM_KEY) AS any_fac_room_key,
      BUILDING_KEY,
      FLOOR_KEY,
      FLOOR,
      -- try to derive a readable floor name from ROOM_FULL_NAME or ROOM if present; keep null if not
      NULLIF(TRIM(ROOM_FULL_NAME), '') AS FLOOR_NAME
    FROM fac_rooms_space_area
    GROUP BY
      BUILDING_KEY,
      FLOOR_KEY,
      FLOOR
  ) AS fr
LEFT JOIN
  -- building dimension (current) to provide canonical building key (FCLT_BUILDING_KEY).
  -- If fac_rooms_space_area.BUILDING_KEY already equals FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, this still works.
  fclt_building_current AS b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fr.BUILDING_KEY OR b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fr.BUILDING_KEY
fclt_floor_per_building.description: Each floor row for facility buildings exposing building linkage (FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) and floor identifier so distinct floor counts can be computed per DLC.

tip_subject_offered_core_27.name: tip_subject_offered_core_27
tip_subject_offered_core_27.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Canonical PK for a TIP subject offered row (carry through if present in source)
  sog.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY` AS `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,

  -- Term code for the offering (lifted from latest section-level summary)
  sog.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,

  -- Primary subject identifier normalized to SUBJECT_ID from the latest subject_offered summary
  sog.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,

  -- Offering department name (preferred from subject_offered latest; falls back to department name from enrollment summary if missing)
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(sog.`OFFER_DEPT_NAME`, ''),
    NULLIF(ssa.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`, '')
  ) AS `OFFER_DEPT_NAME`,

  -- Number of enrolled students for the subject offering.
  -- Prefer NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS carried on the subject_offered_latest_by_section row (section-level copy),
  -- otherwise fall back to aggregated total_subject_enrollment_number from subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject.
  COALESCE(
    sog.`NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`,
    ssa.`total_subject_enrollment_number`,
    0
  ) AS `NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`
FROM
  -- Use the latest-by-section subject offered view as the canonical driving source for TIP subject offerings.
  subject_offered_latest_by_section AS sog
  -- Left-join the subject-level enrollment aggregates (by term+subject) to obtain department/name and enrollment when not present on sog.
  LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject AS ssa
    ON ssa.`TERM_CODE` = sog.`TERM_CODE`
    AND ssa.`SUBJECT_ID` = sog.`SUBJECT_ID`
tip_subject_offered_core_27.description: Canonical row-level view of TIP subjects offered, exposing identifying keys, department, term, and enrollment count. Normalizes the primary identifiers used to join to TIP detail and materials.

tip_detail_to_material_link.name: tip_detail_to_material_link
tip_detail_to_material_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,
  d.`TERM_CODE`,
  d.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`,
  m.`ISBN`
FROM
  -- detail (subject offering -> material link) table assumed to be named `tip_detail`
  `tip_detail` AS d
  -- material table assumed to be named `tip_material` and linked by TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  LEFT JOIN `tip_material` AS m
    ON d.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
  -- also allow linking by ISBN in case TIP_DETAIL stores ISBN but not material key
  LEFT JOIN `tip_material` AS m_isbn
    ON (d.`ISBN` IS NOT NULL AND d.`ISBN` != '' AND m_isbn.`ISBN` = d.`ISBN`)
WHERE
  -- prefer the material matched by TIP_MATERIAL_KEY if present, otherwise fall back to ISBN match
  (m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` IS NOT NULL OR m_isbn.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` IS NOT NULL)
tip_detail_to_material_link.description: Row-level link between TIP subject offerings (detail) and TIP materials. Exposes TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, and ISBN to enable joins to the material table by either key or ISBN.

iap_session_info.name: iap_session_info
iap_session_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  NULLIF(s.SESSION_TITLE, '') AS SESSION_TITLE,
  NULLIF(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '') AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  NULLIF(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '') AS SESSION_END_TIME,

  -- preserve any existing sequence; coerce empty to NULL
  NULLIF(s.SESSION_SEQUENCE, '') AS SESSION_SEQUENCE,
  -- HAS_SESSION_INFO: true (1) if any of the main descriptive fields is non-null/non-empty
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(s.SESSION_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(s.SESSION_START_TIME, ''), NULLIF(s.SESSION_END_TIME, ''), NULLIF(s.SESSION_DATE, ''), NULLIF(s.SESSION_LOCATION, ''), NULLIF(s.SESSION_SEQUENCE, '')) IS NOT NULL
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0

academic_terms_base.name: academic_terms_base
academic_terms_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  `ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,
  `TERM_CODE`,
  `TERM_DESCRIPTION`,
  `IS_CURRENT_TERM`,
  `TERM_START_DATE`
FROM (
  -- Canonical source: prefer academic_terms if present, fall back to academic_terms_all.
  SELECT
    at.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,
    at.`TERM_CODE`,
    at.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`,
    at.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`,
    at.`TERM_START_DATE`
  FROM `academic_terms` at
  WHERE at.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    ata.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,
    ata.`TERM_CODE`,
    ata.`TERM_DESCRIPTION`,
    ata.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`,
    ata.`TERM_START_DATE`
  FROM `academic_terms_all` ata
  WHERE ata.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
    -- Exclude rows already present in academic_terms to avoid duplicates:
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `academic_terms` at2
      WHERE at2.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY` = ata.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`
        AND at2.`TERM_CODE` = ata.`TERM_CODE`
        AND at2.`TERM_START_DATE` = ata.`TERM_START_DATE`
    )
) AS canonical_terms
academic_terms_base.description: Canonical row-per-academic-term with primary term identifiers and metadata (keeps original columns used to identify term and current-term flag).

cis_course_catalog_terms.name: cis_course_catalog_terms
cis_course_catalog_terms.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- If EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE present use it as the TERM_CODE for the row; otherwise NULL.
  c.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- Canonical offering flags taken from cis_course_catalog row. Keep values as-is (string flags).
  c.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM`,
  c.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  c.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog` c
-- Ensure a canonical subject identifier: use MASTER_SUBJECT_ID when available; otherwise fall back to SUBJECT_ID.
-- The required grain is one row per MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,SUBJECT_ID,MASTER_SUBJECT_ID.
-- To preserve that grain we include all cis_course_catalog rows; rows without MASTER_SUBJECT_ID will still
-- appear with MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = SUBJECT_ID (handled by COALESCE below).
-- Replace MASTER_SUBJECT_ID with SUBJECT_ID when NULL to maintain joinability.
WHERE 1=1
  -- no literal filters in view; consumers can filter by TERM_CODE/EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE as needed
cis_course_catalog_terms.description: Normalized CIS course-catalog rows with canonical subject identifier and explicit flags/term-association columns to indicate whether course is offered in a given TERM_CODE. Exposes one row per CIS course record (subject) per effective term-code if available; otherwise row-level course with offering flags.

cis_subject_term_cohort.name: cis_subject_term_cohort
cis_subject_term_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through term identifier
  `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`               AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- distinct subject unique id: prefer MASTER_SUBJECT_ID when present, otherwise SUBJECT_ID
  COALESCE(NULLIF(`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''), `SUBJECT_ID`) AS `SUBJECT_UNIQUE_ID`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog`
WHERE
  -- only include rows that have an effective term code and a subject identifier
  `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` <> ''
  AND (
    (`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '')
    OR (`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `SUBJECT_ID` <> '')
  )
GROUP BY
  `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''), `SUBJECT_ID`)
cis_subject_term_cohort.description: Aggregates cis_course_catalog to one row per TERM_CODE and subject identifier (distinct subject) to support counting distinct CIS course types per term. Does not collapse across terms; produces one row per (TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_UNIQUE_ID).

tip_subject_offered_school.name: tip_subject_offered_school

tip_subject_offered_school.description: Normalized subject-offered rows exposing TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY and the OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME (school for the offering). Useful fallback for school lookups for TIP subjects.

tip_subject_offered_rows.name: tip_subject_offered_rows
tip_subject_offered_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.term_code                                  AS TERM_CODE,
  s.master_subject_id                           AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  s.course_number                               AS COURSE_NUMBER,
  s.subject_id                                  AS SUBJECT_ID,
  s.subject_title                               AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  s.offer_school_name                            AS OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  s.offer_dept_code                              AS OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  s.responsible_faculty_mit_id                   AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  COALESCE(s.num_enrolled_students, se.total_subject_enrollment_number, 0) AS NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  s.subject_offered_summary_key                  AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
FROM
  subject_offered_latest_by_section s
LEFT JOIN
  subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject se
    ON s.term_code = se.term_code
   AND s.subject_id = se.subject_id
WHERE
  -- keep the grain: one row per TIP subject offering (use the master/summary row for each offered subject)
  -- filter to master/subject-level rows (depends on available flags); if IS_MASTER_SECTION exists use it, otherwise include all
  (s.is_master_section = 'Y' OR s.is_master_section IS NULL)
tip_subject_offered_rows.description: One row per TIP subject offering (a TIP subject/course in a given term) exposing identifying fields and offering-level dimensions (department, school, enrollment, responsible faculty, etc.).

tip_material_raw.name: tip_material_raw

SELECT

    UNION ALL

WHERE `TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` IS NOT NULL

tip_subject_offered_raw.name: tip_subject_offered_raw
tip_subject_offered_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT_WS('|', so.`TERM_CODE`, so.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, so.`COURSE_NUMBER`, so.`SECTION_ID`) AS `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,
  so.`TERM_CODE`,

  so.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,

FROM subject_offered_latest_by_section AS so
LEFT JOIN subject_summary_enrollment_agg_by_term_subject AS ssea
  ON ssea.`TERM_CODE` = so.`TERM_CODE`
  AND ssea.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = so.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`

tip_subject_offered_rows_40.name: tip_subject_offered_rows_40

Exposes each tip_subject_offered row (one row per TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) with raw attributes needed for grouping, filtering, and aggregation (term, school offering, enrollment, master/subject ids, responsible faculty).
